fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Pricing Analyst, Merch Planner
fields.Trigger: Seasonal SKU sell-through falls below plan threshold

Automation Opportunity: - Threshold-trigger auto-surfaced as a worklist; markdown-recommendation auto-computed from residual inventory × weeks-remaining
Controls: - CTL-422 (price-change authorization — links to VS-08 / W40 price-change execution); operational: Category Manager markdown approval
Pain Points / Risks: - **Threshold-gaming risk**: a SKU hovers just above the threshold to avoid markdown, accumulating dead stock; mitigated by a trend-based trigger (3 weeks of sub-plan sell-through) alongside the point threshold

- **Markdown-spiral risk**: repeated markdowns erode margin below the vendor-allowance recovery, netting a loss; mitigated by the W2397 reconciliation and the stop-loss floor (clearance-at-cost trigger)
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-57 / W107, VS-64 / W2385 markdown triggers) — the threshold-armed markdown
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-64 / W2387 sell-through monitoring) — the sell-through signal
- POS/label (links to VS-08 / W5B, W181 price-tag) — the price update and label
Time Estimate: ~30 min/decision × ~250 decisions/season × 6 seasons (~750 hours) + ~1–2 hours/decision approval on the ~25% escalated subset per the W93 authorization matrix (~375–750 hours) = **~1,125–1,500 hours/year** Pricing Analyst + Category Manager.

steps.activity: System monitors sell-through vs. plan; auto-flags SKUs below threshold: <40% sold at mid-season, <70% at 75% of season; Pricing Analyst recommends markdown level based on residual inventory and weeks remaining
Category Manager approves markdown; system updates price; POS reflects new price; shelf labels updated; customer communication if significant price reduction

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, Pricing Analyst, Store Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Phase auto-executed on the schedule OR on the sell-through gate (whichever triggers first); phase-effectiveness auto-measured for W2403
Controls: - CTL-422 (price-change authorization); operational: Category Manager phase-definition sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Phase-too-aggressive risk**: phase 2's 25–40% off triggers before phase 1 has cleared its target, compressing margin; mitigated by the phase-gate on sell-through (advance to phase 2 only when phase 1 cleared ≥60%)

- **Phase-too-conservative risk**: phases are too shallow to clear inventory before season end, leaving dead stock for W2393 consolidation; mitigated by the W2397 post-clearance reconciliation feeding the next season's phase-depth model
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-64 / W2390) — the phased markdown schedule
- Promo/label (links to VS-14 / W262, VS-08 / W181) — the clearance signage and labels per phase
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113, W2387) — the sell-through that confirms phase progression
Time Estimate: ~1 day/phase × 3 phases × 6 seasons = **~140–180 hours/year** Merch Planner.

steps.activity: Phase 1 (mid-season): 10–15% off slow movers. Phase 2 (late season): 25–40% off remaining. Phase 3 (final 2 weeks): 50–75% off clearance. Planner defines phases; system executes per schedule

Automation Opportunity: - Clearance-label auto-generated per the W2390/2391 markdown; clearance-zone plan auto-distributed
Controls: - CTL-422 (ensure controlled execution — Markdown & Clearance Execution (PA-64.2).)
- CTL-422 (price-tag accuracy — links to W69); operational: Store Manager clearance-zone setup sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Crowd-safety risk**: a heavily-promoted clearance event draws a crowd that exceeds the zone's safe capacity; mitigated by the customer-flow management and the staffing surge for the event
- **Mis-labeled-item risk**: a non-clearance item is marked clearance (or vice versa), causing a customer dispute or margin leakage; mitigated by the W2395 compliance audit during the event
System Touchpoints: - Marketing/promo (links to VS-14 / W83 campaign, W262 promotional setup) — the clearance-event promotion
- Clearance zone/label (links to VS-55 / W2168, VS-08 / W181) — the clearance-zone setup and labels
- POS (links to VS-08 / W5B, W93 clearance-markdown price) — the clearance-price transaction
Time Estimate: (~6 h execution + ~1–2 h setup) per store per event × 200 stores × 6 events/year ≈ **~8,400–9,600 hours/year** Store teams (absorbed into store-ops surge; × 1.5-week elapsed cycles).

steps.activity: Marketing promotes clearance event (social media, email, in-store signage); Store Manager sets up clearance zone; staff applies clearance labels; manages customer flow during event

fields.Participants: Merch Planner, DC Ops, Store Managers
fields.Volume: ~5–15% of seasonal inventory unsold after clearance

Automation Opportunity: - Remaining inventory auto-flagged post-clearance; disposition auto-suggested per the net-recovery ranking
Controls: - CTL-422 (ensure controlled execution — Markdown & Clearance Execution (PA-64.2).)
- operational: clearance-disposition approval with separate tracking; Category Manager disposition sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dead-stock-blindness risk**: the remaining inventory isn't identified and sits in stores/backrooms, aging into obsolescence; mitigated by the post-clearance remaining-inventory report auto-generated from the inventory system
- **Disposition-suboptimization risk**: inventory that could be donated (tax benefit) is instead scrapped (no benefit); mitigated by the disposition-decision framework ranking options by net recovery
System Touchpoints: - Inventory/disposition (links to VS-05 / W91 damaged/obsolete, W220 slow-moving, VS-32 returns) — the remaining-inventory identification and disposition
- Transfers (links to VS-05 / W22 store transfers, W154 rebalancing) — the cross-store consolidation
- Vendor return (links to VS-03 / W88 RTV, VS-64 / W2388 markdown agreement) — the vendor return/swap
Time Estimate: ~1.5 weeks/season × 6 seasons = **~350–500 hours/year** Merch Planner + DC Ops.

steps.activity: Planner identifies remaining clearance inventory across stores; determines disposition: (a) transfer to stores still selling (regional variation), (b) consolidate at DC for bulk sale to discount buyers, (c) return to vendor per markdown agreement, (d) donate for tax benefit

Automation Opportunity: - Allowance auto-calculated from the unsold quantity × agreement rate; vendor-claim auto-generated with evidence pack
Controls: - CTL-39: rebate/allowance accuracy; CTL-44 (duplicate-claim guard); operational: Finance Manager sign-off on the claim
Pain Points / Risks: - **Quantity-dispute risk**: the vendor disputes the unsold-quantity claim (argues BuildRight over-ordered); mitigated by the documented PO-vs-sell-through evidence and the W2388 agreement term

- **Allowance-non-recovery risk**: the vendor delays or denies the credit and BuildRight writes off the markdown without recovery; mitigated by the CTL-48 dispute-resolution workflow and the allowance-aging tracker
System Touchpoints: - Co-op/rebate (links to VS-39 / W27, VS-64 / W2388 markdown-support term) — the allowance agreement
- AP (links to VS-15 / W7, W7C) — the vendor credit recording
- Inventory (links to VS-05 / W91, VS-64 / W2393) — the unsold-quantity basis
Time Estimate: ~2.5 days/season × 6 seasons across ~75 vendors = **~150–200 hours/year** Finance Analyst.

steps.activity: Finance calculates vendor markdown allowance per agreement: unsold inventory × agreed support %; submits claim to vendor; vendor validates and credits; Finance records in AP

fields.Participants: Merch Coord, Store Manager, Regional Ops

Automation Opportunity: - Clearance-label vs. system-price auto-compared via RF-gun scan (links to W2176 pattern)
Controls: - CTL-422 (price-tag accuracy — links to W69); operational: Merchandising Coordinator per-event sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-trust risk**: a clearance label that doesn't ring up at the labeled price erodes trust and risks a DTI complaint (W2682); mitigated by the on-the-spot correction and the ≥99% price-accuracy target
- **Margin-leakage risk**: a non-clearance item is incorrectly marked clearance, leaking margin; mitigated by the audit catching the mis-label
System Touchpoints: - Compliance system (links to VS-55 / W2174, VS-177 field audit) — the clearance-compliance check
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-64 / W2390/2391) — the authorized clearance price
- POS (links to VS-08 / W5B, W93) — the transaction price
Time Estimate: ~2.5 hours/event × 6 events + per-store checks absorbed = **~100–150 hours/year** Coordinator + Regional Ops.

steps.activity: Coordinator verifies: clearance prices match system, clearance labels applied, clearance zone properly merchandised, non-clearance items not incorrectly discounted; non-compliance corrected immediately

Automation Opportunity: - Employee-discount auto-applied on clearance SKUs during the event window; eligibility auto-verified from HRIS
Controls: - CTL-422 (ensure controlled execution — Markdown & Clearance Execution (PA-64.2).)
- CTL-422 (employee-purchase controls — links to W205); operational: Store Manager event-execution sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Abuse risk**: an employee purchases for resale (not personal use), violating the program intent; mitigated by quantity limits per employee and the W205 employee-purchase controls

- **Stockout-for-public risk**: the employee event clears inventory that public customers would have bought, displacing public revenue; mitigated by the employee event sequenced after the public clearance completes
System Touchpoints: - POS/employee discount (links to VS-08 / W205 employee purchase, POS-022) — the employee-discount-on-clearance application
- HRIS (links to VS-19 / W292 employee master) — the eligibility verification
- Inventory (links to VS-64 / W2393 remaining clearance) — the eligible inventory
Time Estimate: ~1 day/event × 6 events + ~2 hours/store event = **~200–300 hours/year** HR + Store teams.

steps.activity: HR coordinates employee clearance event: additional 20–30% off remaining clearance for employees; store opens early or designates specific hours; system applies employee discount on clearance price

fields.Participants: Finance Mgr, Category Mgr, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - Seasonal P&L auto-assembled from the cost/markdown/allowance/revenue datasets; variance-vs-plan auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-422 (ensure controlled execution — Markdown & Clearance Execution (PA-64.2).)
- operational: allowance accuracy; CTL-176 (clearance events reconciled financially post-event — COGS accuracy owned with VS-158); operational: CFO sign-off on the seasonal P&L
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-distortion risk**: the reconciliation conflates seasonal margin with regular-category margin, hiding a seasonal-category loss; mitigated by the seasonal-category P&L isolated per W2404

- **Allowance-timing risk**: the vendor allowance is recorded in a different period than the markdown, distorting the period margin; mitigated by the allowance-accrual at markdown time (not waiting for the vendor credit)
System Touchpoints: - Cost accounting (links to VS-158 / W85, VS-17 / W26 budget) — the seasonal-category P&L
- Co-op/allowance (links to VS-39 / W27, VS-64 / W2394) — the vendor-allowance recovery
- Inventory write-off (links to VS-05 / W91, VS-64 / W2393) — the unrecovered remainder

steps.activity: Finance reconciles: seasonal inventory cost, markdown cost, vendor allowance, clearance revenue, net margin on seasonal category; calculates seasonal category profitability vs. plan
